remediations.title: Disable SMBv1 Entirely
remediations.recommendation: Remove the SMBv1 protocol from the server. It has no place on a modern network and is required by no supported application.
steps: Disable-WindowsOptionalFeature -Online -FeatureName SMB1Protocol
Alternatively: Set-SmbServerConfiguration -EnableSMB1Protocol $false
Reboot the host and re-run this scanner to confirm the SMBv1 Detector module now reports smb1_enabled=false
Block legacy SMBv1 negotiation at the network layer (firewall/IPS) as defense-in-depth for hosts that cannot be patched immediately

remediations.title: Enforce SMB Message Signing
remediations.recommendation: Require SMB signing on both the client and server side so that relayed or tampered authentication attempts are rejected.
steps: Set-SmbServerConfiguration -RequireSecuritySignature $true
Set-SmbClientConfiguration -RequireSecuritySignature $true
Enforce via Group Policy: Computer Configuration > Windows Settings > Security Settings > Local Policies > Security Options > 'Microsoft network server: Digitally sign communications (always)'
Prioritize Domain Controllers and Tier-0 assets first, then expand to the rest of the fleet

remediations.title: Enable SMB 3.x Transport Encryption
remediations.recommendation: Upgrade or reconfigure the SMB stack so SMB 3.x encryption is negotiable, then enforce it for sensitive shares.
steps: Confirm the host OS supports SMB 3.x encryption (Windows Server 2012 or later)
Set-SmbServerConfiguration -EncryptData $true
For per-share enforcement: Set-SmbShare -Name <ShareName> -EncryptData $true
Verify with this scanner that encryption_state reports 'required' after the change

remediations.title: Make SMB Encryption Mandatory, Not Optional
remediations.recommendation: Encryption capability exists but is not enforced. Flip enforcement on so every session is protected rather than only sessions that opt in.
steps: Set-SmbServerConfiguration -EncryptData $true -RejectUnencryptedAccess $true
For per-share enforcement: Set-SmbShare -Name <ShareName> -EncryptData $true
Re-scan to confirm encryption_state now reports 'required'

remediations.title: Restrict The Minimum Negotiable SMB Dialect
remediations.recommendation: Prevent the server from accepting legacy SMB 2.0.2 negotiation so an on-path attacker cannot strip the session down to a weaker dialect.
steps: Set-SmbServerConfiguration -EnableSMB2Protocol $true (keep SMB2+ enabled)
Where business requirements allow, raise the minimum accepted dialect via Group Policy or registry to exclude SMB 2.0.2
Pair this with mandatory signing and encryption so a downgraded session is still protected
Validate with this scanner that downgrade_possible reports false after remediation

remediations.title: Disable Guest Session Fallback
remediations.recommendation: Prevent the server from silently falling back to a guest-equivalent session for unrecognized or blank credentials.
steps: Set-SmbServerConfiguration -EnableInsecureGuestLogons $false
Enforce via Group Policy: 'Microsoft network server: Allow insecure guest logons' = Disabled
Audit local accounts to ensure a Guest account is not inadvertently enabled
Re-scan to confirm guest_access_allowed reports false

remediations.title: Restrict Anonymous (Null Session) Access
remediations.recommendation: Eliminate the ability to establish an unauthenticated session, which removes an entire class of pre-authentication enumeration.
steps: Set the 'Network access: Restrict anonymous access to Named Pipes and Shares' Group Policy setting to Enabled
Set 'Network access: Do not allow anonymous enumeration of SAM accounts' and the 'and shares' variant to Enabled
Review the RestrictNullSessAccess, NullSessionPipes and NullSessionShares registry values under HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\LanManServer\Parameters
Re-scan to confirm session_is_null reports false
references: CIS Microsoft Windows Server Benchmark: Network Access controls

remediations.title: Lock Down Administrative Share Access
remediations.recommendation: Ensure ADMIN$, C$ and IPC$ are only reachable by accounts that are explicitly authorized local or domain administrators, never by guest or low-privilege sessions.
steps: Confirm no guest or null session can authenticate at all (see the guest_access_allowed and null_session_allowed remediations, which remove the precondition for this finding)
Review local Administrators group membership and remove unnecessary members
Where administrative shares are not required operationally, disable them via the AutoShareServer/AutoShareWks registry values
Deploy Windows Defender Credential Guard and LAPS to reduce the value of any credential that does reach this host

remediations.title: Suppress Pre-Authentication OS Version Disclosure
remediations.recommendation: Reduce the amount of fingerprinting information handed to unauthenticated clients during NTLM negotiation.
steps: Set the registry value HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa\MSV1_0 to suppress the OS version in the NTLM NegotiateFlags where supported by the OS version
Treat this as a defense-in-depth measure, not a substitute for patching; attackers can often fingerprint builds through other means
Prioritize this only after the higher-severity findings on this report are closed

remediations.title: Rotate And Harden The Validated Credential
remediations.recommendation: The supplied credential authenticated successfully, which this assessment should treat as a confirmed compromised or weak credential requiring immediate action.
steps: Rotate the password or NTLM hash for this account immediately
Review the account's privilege level and remove unnecessary group memberships, especially local administrator or domain-privileged roles
Enable multi-factor authentication or a compensating control for interactive logon paths tied to this identity where available
Audit authentication logs for this account for prior unauthorized use

remediations.title: Verify Patch Level Against CVE-2020-0796
remediations.recommendation: Compression support alone is not a vulnerability; confirm the host has the March 2020 or later cumulative update applied.
steps: Check the installed Windows build and cumulative update level against Microsoft Security Advisory ADV200005
If the host cannot be patched immediately, disable SMB compression as a temporary mitigation: Set-SmbServerConfiguration -DisableCompression $true
Re-enable compression once the patch is confirmed installed, since disabling it is a workaround, not a fix

remediations.title: Validate Target Identity Before Further Testing
remediations.recommendation: Manually verify this host is the intended, legitimate target before continuing assessment or remediation work against it.
steps: Cross-check the host's inventory record (asset management / CMDB) against the IP and hostname reported by this scan
If the host is unexpected or unrecognized, treat it as a potential honeypot or rogue device and escalate to the network/security team
Re-run the scan from a different vantage point to confirm the inconsistency is not a transient network artifact
